Hi Alice — great talking to you and Bob. Short answers up front, then a proposed POC scope: 

1) Capacity guarantees: Redwood Dedicated provides reserved GPU pools with SLA-backed throughput and latency SLOs. For your concurrency profile (120 concurrent sessions, bursts to 200), we can reserve a pool sized to hold steady-state plus burst capacity; we expose a per-second and per-minute throughput metric and a provisioning SLA (we commit to <5% request rejection during provisioned capacity).

2) Hyperscaler comparison: buying raw instances on a hyperscaler gives you raw compute but typically lacks the inference optimizations (continuous batching, KV cache management, optimized kernels) we run in the runtime. That means higher per-token cost at your request distribution and more engineering ops overhead (autoscaling tuning, GPU memory management). Practically: for the same 99th-pctl latency target and your model family, we project 20–35% lower total unit cost on Redwood Dedicated vs self-managed instances after accounting for engineering and caching.

3) 2-week POC: propose the following steps:
  - Week 0: contract/NDAs + firewall rules + sample dataset ingestion
  - Week 1: baseline on hyperscaler (you run your current stack) + Redwood side fully instrumented replicate run
  - Week 2: run mixed workload (peak simulation) & handover report + knob tuning (batching, cache TTLs, quantization profile)

Action items I propose:
- I will share a one-page POC plan and the Redwood load-test script.
- Dylan will schedule capacity sizing sync with your infra team.
- Lauren will prepare a draft SLA and pricing sheet for dedicated reservation options.

I'll attach the Dedicated pricing PDF and a draft SLA. Happy to chat tomorrow if that's easier.

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf; capacity-sla-draft.docx

Hi Bob / Alice — quick answers and proposed test artifacts below. Happy to jump on a call.

Latency/cost snapshot (rough, for Athena-7B quantized, 512 token responses):
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool, optimized runtime): p50 30ms, p95 150ms, p99 320ms; estimated unit cost $0.0009 per response (includes caching benefits).
- Redwood Hosted (shared pool + prefix caching): p50 40ms, p95 200ms, p99 420ms; unit cost $0.0014 per response.
- Self-managed hyperscaler (EC2 fleet, tuned): p50 45ms, p95 240ms, p99 600ms; unit cost $0.0018 per response (engineering ops excluded).

Burst-to-hyperscaler pre-warm: Redwood can own pre-warming as an add-on — we will provision standby instances and keep them warm for a fee; we can guarantee instance availability per a burst SLA if the capacity is reserved. If relying on on-demand hyperscaler instances without our managed warm pool, we cannot guarantee sub-minute availability.

Security: for Dedicated/Private we keep KV cache and logs inside your VPC (or on-prem), we can add a contract clause.

Proposed quick tests (to run in parallel week 1):
1) Baseline run on your fleet (you export telemetry).
2) Redwood replicate: run same traces against a Redwood Dedicated sandbox with our load-test script (attached).
3) Tail latency test: 1h stepwise ramp to 3x baseline to validate p99 behavior and request rejection rates.

I'll attach the load-test script and a short README. Can we do a 30m sync tomorrow 11am PT?

Regards,
Dylan
Principal Solutions Engineer

Attachments: load-test-script.sh; readme-loadtest.md
